theorem: Let phi: R -> S be a ring homomorphism. Then ker(phi) is an ideal of R.
assumptions: phi: R -> S is a ring homomorphism

proof_steps.text: Let a and b be in ker(phi). Then phi(a) = 0 and phi(b) = 0.
We have phi(a - b) = phi(a) - phi(b) = 0, so a - b is in ker(phi).
Thus ker(phi) is closed under subtraction.

Because phi(0_R) = 0_S, the kernel is nonempty; together with closure under subtraction, this makes ker(phi) an additive subgroup of R. If r is in R and x is in ker(phi), then phi(rx) = phi(r)phi(x) = 0 and phi(xr) = phi(x)phi(r) = 0, so rx and xr are in ker(phi). Therefore ker(phi) is a two-sided ideal of R.
